title: Tenant token buckets and adaptive eviction policy for load shedding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We need a predictable, tenant-aware load shedding mechanism that enforces SLOs during regional capacity pressure and multi-region failover. Current runtime admission logic is coarse-grained and can cause single noisy tenants or bursty workloads to push other customers into SLA violations. This ticket proposes hierarchical token buckets (global -> region -> tenant) combined with an adaptive eviction score and soft-degradation strategies (response truncation, degraded features) and a circuit-breaker hook for critical routes. Goals: 1) Prevent a single tenant from causing region-wide SLO breaches; 2) Maintain graceful degradation with measurable quality loss; 3) Provide fast, observable indicators for on-call and automated failover logic.
acceptance_criteria: Hierarchical token buckets enforced in runtime: global, regional, tenant levels with configurable refill rates and burst sizes
Eviction score computed per request including tenant credit, request priority, recent error rate, and SLO risk factor
Soft-degradation modes implemented and selectable per route: truncate-response, fast-fallback-model, disable-noncritical-plugins
Circuit-breaker integration: trip on sustained latency or error spikes and fallback to lower-cost model variants
End-to-end tests simulating noisy-tenant failure show <1% SLO violation for unaffected tenants in Canary region
Metrics and dashboards: per-tenant shed rate, token balance, eviction decisions, and incident alerts are present in console
Canary rollout completed with automated rollback on >0.5% customer-impacting errors
implementation_notes: Token bucket hierarchy will be implemented inside admission controller module to minimize cross-service calls
Persist tenant token state in local region in-memory store with periodic snapshots to Redis for reconciliation
Eviction score = w1*(1 - tenant_token_fraction) + w2*priority_penalty + w3*recent_error_rate + w4*region_slo_pressure. We will start with w1=0.5,w2=0.2,w3=0.2,w4=0.1 and tune from telemetry
Soft-degradation actions are pluggable: each route has an ordered list of degradation handlers. Handlers must be idempotent and report degradation telemetry
Circuit-breaker states expose debug endpoints and use sliding-window metrics for decisioning (p95 latency, error_rate over 1m/5m windows)
Config flags: feature gate 'tenant_shed_v2' and per-customer overrides for priority tiers (enterprise/free)
test_plan: Unit tests for token accounting including refills and concurrent consumes
Integration test: synthetic workload generator with 100 tenants, inject one noisy tenant producing 10x traffic spike and assert unaffected tenants keep SLOs
Chaos test: kill regional inference pool while shedding active traffic and verify multi-region reroute does not double-charge tenant tokens
Load test: measure overhead added to admission latency; target <0.5ms median increase
Canary scenario using 5% of traffic for 2 hours with active telemetry assertions
rollout_plan: Feature flag rollout: enable in staging -> internal prod orgs -> 5% canary -> 25% -> 100%
Observation window at each step: 2 hours for 5%, 6 hours for 25%
Automated rollback triggers: increase in global SLO violations, customer_error_increase > 0.5%, token accounting mismatch > 0.1%
Post-rollout audit: run reconciliation job to compare in-memory vs Redis snapshots and publish results to oncall channel
Documentation: add runbook section for oncall about interpreting token/eviction metrics and manual override instructions
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Token accounting mismatch during region failover could temporarily allow over-consumption. Mitigation: conservative refill limits during failover, and reconciliation job with corrective drains
Risk: Eviction decisions unfair to low-volume high-value customers. Mitigation: per-tenant priority tiers and allowlist for critical tenants; billing/comm SLA safeguards
Risk: Added admission latency. Mitigation: implement lightweight heuristics in hot path, expensive scoring in best-effort path and cache scores per-request-hash
Risk: Complexity of soft-degradation handlers causing subtle regressions. Mitigation: require handlers to have unit+integration tests and a single rollback flag to disable all degradations
